title: Analysis of factors hindering the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: A qualitative study
content:
by Cuicui Dou, Yi Sun, Keke Dai, Man Wei, Jiawen Li, Kaili Qu, Qiongyan Hu, Huiyan Zhang

Background

Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) have a high incidence of perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression of thermoregulation, prolonged surgical duration, and diminished endogenous thermoregulatory function, which can lead to poor outcomes. Effective prevention of hypothermia is a critical clinical issue; however, previous studies have lacked in-depth analysis of comprehensive continuous management and practical barriers.

Objective

This study aimed to identify barriers to the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients.

Methods

A qualitative study design was employed, conducted from January to February 2026 at a Grade III Level A hospital in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Using purposive sampling, anesthesiologists (n = 5), anesthesia nurses (n = 5), and operating room nurses (n = 5) were recruited as participants. Semi-structured face-to-face interviews were conducted, and data were analyzed using content analysis with the assistance of NVivo 12.0 software.

Results

A total of 3 themes and 5 subthemes were identified: (1) System and process level: The warm chain management process requires improvement, and the allocation of key warming resources needs to be strengthened; (2) Human resources and team atmosphere level: Nursing staffing needs to be reinforced, and a positive organizational culture requires cultivation; (3) Multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous improvement level: The multidisciplinary collaboration platform and continuous improvement system remain inadequate.

Conclusion

Diverse factors hinder the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients. Managers should implement improvements across three dimensions—system processes, human resources and team atmosphere, and multidisciplinary collaboration—to explore perioperative temperature management strategies and promote quality improvements in hypothermia prevention and control.
author: Cuicui Dou
